name: Etoposide
route_note: IV infusion; oral capsules (about half as bioavailable); etoposide phosphate is a water-soluble IV prodrug

discovery.note: A semisynthetic glycoside derivative of podophyllotoxin from the mayapple (Podophyllum).

tagline: Mayapple-derived topoisomerase II poison used in testicular and lung cancer
summary: Etoposide is a semisynthetic podophyllotoxin derivative that stabilises the topoisomerase II–DNA complex, causing double-strand breaks. It is used in testicular cancer, small-cell lung cancer, lymphomas and leukaemias, and in high-dose transplant conditioning.
mechanism: Unlike its parent podophyllotoxin (a tubulin binder), etoposide acts on topoisomerase II. It forms a ternary complex with the enzyme and cleaved DNA, preventing re-ligation of the double-strand break.

Accumulated breaks trigger apoptosis, mainly in late S and G2 phase. Inhibition of topoisomerase II and the resulting chromosomal translocations (often involving KMT2A/MLL) underlie therapy-related leukaemias.

history.title: Clinical trials
history.detail: First clinical studies begin in Europe.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as VePesid (Bristol-Myers) for refractory testicular cancer.

history.title: Mechanism
history.detail: Topoisomerase II is identified as the target of epipodophyllotoxins.

history.title: BEP
history.detail: Williams et al. show BEP (bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin) is less toxic than PVB with equal efficacy in testicular cancer.

safety.boxed_warning: US labels carry a boxed warning about severe myelosuppression and use by experienced physicians.

facts: The 'VP' in VP-16 refers to its origin as a podophyllotoxin derivative.
